title: Jurisdictional Lockbox: Automated Evidence Capture & Retention Assertion Bridge
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers in regulated jurisdictions require automated, auditable proof that their data and related artifacts are stored, retained, and purged according to region-specific policies. Current manual evidence collection is error-prone, slow during audits, and causes delays for Dedicated/Private onboarding.

Goal: Build a lightweight, auditable 'Lockbox Bridge' that automates collection of control artifacts (logs, config snapshots, retention assertions, KMS key metadata) tagged by jurisdiction, exposes canonical proof bundles for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 evidence requests, and enforces configured retention TTLs per-customer and per-region.

Scope: This ticket covers product design, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the capture/metadata schema, the collector adapter spec (S3/GCS/Blob connectors + runtime agents for on-prem), and the console UX for evidence browsing and ad-hoc attestations. Implementation will be delivered as: (1) a collector microservice (lockbox-collector) running in Redwood Private and Hosted modes, (2) a canonical evidence store with region-tagging & tamper-evident hashes, (3) console + API endpoints to request and download proof bundles, and (4) retention enforcement hooks integrated with the infra cleanup pipeline.

Non-goals: This ticket does not include full archival cold storage lifecycle policies (separate initiative) or per-customer legal attestation wording (legal team deliverable).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Control-to-evidence mapping exists for SOC 2 CC6 and ISO 27001 Annex A controls impacted by data residency/retention and is published in Confluence.
A2: Collector can ingest artifact types (config snapshot, access log segment, KMS key metadata, consent record) and tag them with 'jurisdiction' and 'retention_policy_id'.
A3: Evidence bundles can be generated via API/Console within 2 minutes for a single customer-region request and include SHA256 manifest for tamper evidence.
A4: Retention enforcement prevents retrieval of artifacts beyond their configured TTL and surfaces purge events in audit logs with proof-of-deletion hashes.
A5: Security review completed with checklist items resolved and security sign-off recorded in the ticket.
A6: End-to-end integration tests (Hosted + Private adapter) pass in CI and a canary customer (internal test org) successfully receives an automated audit bundle.
tasks: T1: Finalize control map for applicable SOC2/ISO27001 controls with Compliance SME and publish mapping doc.
T2: Define canonical evidence schema (manifest format, artifact metadata fields, hash algorithm) and version it.
T3: Design collector adapter API (S3/GCS/Azure + on-prem agent) and retention_policy_id reference model.
T4: Build lockbox-collector service (ingest, tag, store, manifest generation) and skeleton RBAC rules.
T5: Add retention enforcement hook into infra cleanup job and implement proof-of-deletion recording.
T6: Console/UI: evidence browser, region filter, generate attestations button, and download bundle UX.
T7: Security review and threat model; remediate findings from SAST/pen test.
T8: Integration tests, canary rollout plan, and runbook for support/incident handling.
T9: Documentation: API spec, quickstart for Dedicated/Private customers, Confluence runbook for audits.
